claim_support.claim: The original method selects source spans, clusters them into a sentence plan, and generates sequentially; its ICL implementation already string-matches spans and discards unfound spans.
claim_support.evidence: Downloaded published PDF pp. 3-5, Sections 3.1-3.3; pp. 5-8 evaluate generation, attribution and verification effort. This is the baseline feature inventory, not a domain extension.

claim_support.claim: Default Assistant explicitly uses attribution-first cited generation for requirement-level legal case review, adds quote/table relocation, legal subrequirement dependencies and human-assistance evaluation.
claim_support.evidence: Downloaded arXiv v1 PDF pp. 4-6: seven requirements; LangGraph dependencies; quote/table extraction, fuzzy/regex source relocation and copying; 66 law-student participants, accuracy +5.3 pp and time -25.9%. The whole-system comparison does not isolate attribution-first effects.

claim_support.claim: Spectrum shares the attribution-first paradigm and studies quotation-to-abstraction trade-offs on medical, simplification, multihop and general QA tasks.
claim_support.evidence: Downloaded v1 PDF pp. 5-8, Sections 4.1-5.3: shared quotes, quoted generation and revisions; 480 queries and 31 MTurk annotators. Section 6.2 discusses MASH concision; Section 10.1 explicitly identifies the shared paradigm. Perceived utility is not clinical correctness.

claim_support.claim: Generation Programs extends explicit planning with executable trees, source-sentence inputs, instruction-bearing text modules and selective module-level entailment refinement.
claim_support.evidence: Downloaded v1 PDF pp. 2-5, Sections 2.1-2.4; pp. 6-9, Tables 1-3 and Section 4.3. It discusses Attribute First and SummarizationPrograms; the main reported baseline is ALCE, so results do not establish superiority over AfG.

claim_support.claim: AgentGEO implements an attribution-first evaluation engine but adds a webpage diagnose-repair optimizer and document-centric held-out query benchmark.
claim_support.evidence: Downloaded PDF pp. 3-8, Sections 3-6 and Table 2; pp. 33-35 Appendix E.5 has sentence/chunk-index selection, evidence clustering and generation prompts. Citation rate measures webpage visibility; lexical faithfulness measures preservation of the edited page.

claim_support.claim: MedGraphRAG adds medical entity/source/definition graphs and hierarchical retrieval/refinement; Attribute First is a comparison baseline, not the described core algorithm.
claim_support.evidence: Published PDF pp. 2-6: Sections 2.1-2.2 describe triple graph linking and U-Retrieval; Section 3.3.2 compares ATTR-FIRST and reports 7 clinicians plus 5 laypersons. Sections 3.1-3.2 specify the medical QA/fact-checking data and models.

claim_support.claim: FinRAGBench-V/RGenCite adds visual page/block citations and financial multimodal evaluation, but generates answers and citations simultaneously and cites AfG as background.
claim_support.evidence: Published PDF p. 3 Section 2 credits VISA for the visual citation adaptation; pp. 3-6 Sections 3-6 define simultaneous generation, page/block coordinates and metrics; p. 5 reports 1,394 inspected QA pairs. This is not evidence of an AfG domain adoption.

claim_support.claim: CiteLab reproduces AfG as one workflow and adds modular composition, multigranularity diagnostic attribution and interactive workflow improvement.
claim_support.evidence: Published PDF pp. 2-6 Sections 3-4 and Figure 1; Appendix A explains its AfG baseline. Eleven baselines on ASQA are evaluated. The demonstration improves a self-RAG workflow; it does not show a specialized AfG domain adaptation.

claim_support.claim: LLM Specialists studies quality-filtered evidence-based QA training and transfer to sustainability-report and climate QA; its inference is source-conditioned cited generation rather than an AfG staged implementation.
claim_support.evidence: Published PDF pp. 2-5 Sections 2-4: source/format/entailment quality, relevant and irrelevant evidence, dual AttrScore filters, synthetic datasets, ChatReport and ClimateQA held-out use cases. No AfG or Slobodkin match was found in the extracted full text.

claim_support.claim: FRONT is a closely related grounding-before-answer training method that adds synthetic attribution data and consistency-aware DPO alignment; direct derivation from AfG is not established.
claim_support.evidence: Published PDF pp. 2-5 Sections 3.1-3.2: grounding quotes preceding answer tokens, supervised fine-tuning and DPO under shared grounding; ALCE evaluation on ASQA/ELI5/QAMPARI. No Slobodkin or AfG match was found in this PDF.

claim_support.claim: The forensic report workflow separates trace-ID-bearing per-part evidence analysis from actor/role/timeline synthesis and evaluates multiple forensic dimensions; direct AfG lineage is not established.
claim_support.evidence: Freshly downloaded 10-page author manuscript pp. 3-6 Sections 3.2 and 4.2-4.5. P2 extracts timestamp/participants/fact/TraceID records; P3 builds actor and timeline views. Sections 4.1 and 4.5 conflict on manual gold verification; Section 4.5 explicitly says it was not performed. Publisher metadata is separate from this manuscript version.

claim_support.claim: QASemConsistency localizes semantic support errors through predicate-argument QA propositions; it is an evaluator rather than an attribution-first generator.
claim_support.evidence: Published PDF pp. 2-5 Sections 2-4 explain decomposition and support labels; pp. 6-10 describe annotations and automatic entailment models. This supports the distinction between source occurrence, lexical coverage and semantic role correctness.
